name: MDPV
summary: MDPV is a potent stimulant, that often promotes compulsive behavior and euphoric effects. The drug is reported to share similar empathogenic effects with MDMA. There are an abnormally high amount of psychosis cases associated with MDPV. MDPV has been found in products sold as "bath salts", "plant food/fertilizer", and in products sold as "MDMA."

pharmacology.text: MDPV acts as a potent norepinephrine–dopamine reuptake inhibitor (NDRI). Its IC50 for monoamine reuptake inhibition were 4.1 nM for dopamine, 26 nM for norepinephrine, and 3,349 nM for serotonin in rat brain synaptosomes. Similarly, MDPV's IC50 values for monoamine reuptake inhibition were 10 nM for dopamine, 80 nM for norepinephrine, and 2,860 nM for serotonin in human embryonic kidney 293 (HEK293) cells expressing the monoamine transporters.

uses.text: MDPV was first developed in the 1960s by a team at Boehringer Ingelheim. It was claimed to have potential to be an alternative for racemic amphetamine and, despite showing some desirable qualities such as reduced toxicity as compared to amphetamine, was chosen to not be developed as a medicinal drug.
